FINES CO-PRODUCT: Spheronization fines are not wasted — they are sold as:
  - Expandable graphite (flame retardant, building materials)
  - Graphite lubricants and dry lubricants
  - Carbon black feedstock / thermal graphite
  If system expansion is applied for fines co-product, effective graphite burden
  to battery supply chain decreases. Most published LCAs use cut-off method (ignore
  fines co-product credit), making this a conservative upper-bound for graphite load.
Purification after spheronization: thermal (2800°C Acheson furnace) or chemical
  (HF/HCl acid wash) -> final product >99.95% Cg. Yield ~95-98% in purification step.
uncertainty_method: F051 = F052 / spheronization_yield. Spheronization yield range: 40-60%. This is the DOMINANT UNCERTAINTY in graphite chain. At 40% yield: 0.89/0.40 = 2.225 -> high end. At 60% yield: 0.89/0.60 = 1.483 -> low end. High bound 2.65 includes additional purification losses (~5%). Low bound 1.48 assumes 60% spheronization yield (optimistic industrial scenario). GREET 2023 uses 44% spheronization yield -> F051 = 0.89/0.44 = 2.02 kg/kWh (close). Degen 2023: footnotes ~44-52% yield from flake to SPNG. Pell 2021: ~50% yield (less conservative) -> 0.89/0.50 = 1.78 kg/kWh.

notes:
DERIVATION (ELEMENTAL BASIS, Policy 2):
  Li per kWh in CAM = 1.435 × 7.134% = 0.1024 kg Li/kWh (stoichiometric anchor).
  Hydromet recovery from black mass: 80-90% (Harper 2019; central 85%).
  Recovered Li mass (elemental) = 0.1024 × 0.85 ≈ 0.0875 kg/kWh.
Reported on ELEMENTAL BASIS per project convention (Policy 2, 2026-04-30):
  kg of contained Li metal, not kg of LiOH·H2O / Li2CO3 compound. This matches
  industry recovery-rate reporting conventions ("Li recovery 85%" means 85% of
  contained Li, not 85% of compound salt). Conversion to compound for downstream
  re-feed: × 6.05 (1/0.16541) for LiOH·H2O eq, or × 5.32 for Li2CO3 eq.
Hydromet route dominant for NMC811 EoL: shred -> black mass -> H2SO4 leach ->
  SX/IX -> NiSO4/CoSO4/MnSO4 + Li2SO4 -> Li2CO3 or LiOH precipitation.
Pyrometallurgy (Umicore, Glencore) loses Li to slag/dust → only ~50% Li recovery;
  not the dominant route for new NMC plants but historically common.
EU Battery Regulation 2023 mandates 80% Li recovery by 2031, 95% Ni/Co/Cu/Li by 2031
  (with intermediate 50% Li by 2027). Industry investments converging toward hydromet.
Recycled Li offsets primary Li demand at chem_processing node.
uncertainty_method: ELEMENTAL BASIS (Policy 2, project-wide convention 2026-04-30). Li in CAM = 0.1024 kg Li/kWh (= 1.435 × 0.07134, see F003 derivation). notes:
DERIVATION (ELEMENTAL BASIS, Policy 2): Mass-balance closure from EoL pack:
  F100 (5.30) - F101 Li elemental (0.0875) - F102 Ni elemental (0.658)
             - F103 Co elemental (0.0825) = 4.47 kg/kWh residues.
Physical origin of residues:
  - Graphite anode: not recovered at commercial scale (~0.89 kg/kWh).
    Direct recycling and Duesenfeld thermal regeneration are pilot-scale only;
    commercial graphite recovery <5% as of 2024 (cf. AUDIT_NMC_LFP_GRAPHITE_RECOVERY).
  - Electrolyte: ~0.68 kg/kWh; LiPF6 destroyed (HF + LiF + PF5 hazardous);
    carbonate solvents partially recovered by distillation in advanced plants but
    mostly incinerated for energy. Net contribution to F104 ~0.68 kg/kWh.
  - Mn: ~0.08 kg/kWh; lost to leach residue or slag; no battery-grade Mn recovery
    established. (Mn is in CAM but not in F101–F103 since project does not yet model
    Mn recovery loop.)
  - Separator (PE/PP) + cell binders + conductive carbon: ~0.10 kg/kWh; incinerated.
  - Cell can/header (steel, ~0.10 kg) + module/pack structural metal (~1.70 kg of
    Al/steel/plastic) — physically recyclable as metallic scrap but does not
    re-enter the battery supply chain; tracked here as "lost from battery loop".
  - Process residue from incomplete metal recovery: ~5–15% of input Li/Ni/Co stays
    in the leach residue / slag (~0.05 kg/kWh of metal not in F101–F103).
  - Water of hydration, residual sulfate/carbonate fines, miscellaneous: balance.
EU Battery Regulation 2023 graphite/Mn targets are weaker than for Ni/Co/Li/Cu;
  F104 mass is expected to decline toward 2030s as direct-recycling matures and
  graphite recovery becomes commercial.
ELEMENTAL BASIS NOTE: F104 now closes cleanly with F100 because F101–F103 report
  contained metal mass (not compound salt mass). Process-added anion/water mass
  from hydromet chemistry (SO4/OH/H2O) is NOT counted here since it is added during
  recycling and is not part of the EoL pack physical mass.
uncertainty_method:
ELEMENTAL BASIS CLOSURE (Policy 2, project-wide convention 2026-04-30):
  F104 = F100 - F101_elemental - F102_elemental - F103_elemental
       = 5.30 - 0.0875 - 0.658 - 0.0825 = 4.472 kg/kWh.
Now that F101–F103 are reported on elemental basis (kg of contained metal), F104 captures essentially everything in the EoL pack except the recovered metals: graphite, electrolyte (mostly destroyed), separator/binders, Mn (unrecovered), cell can/header steel, and pack structural Al/steel/plastic. Components (by physical origin):
  - Graphite anode (mostly unrecovered): 0.89 kg/kWh
  - Electrolyte (incinerated/destroyed in solvent recovery): 0.68 kg/kWh
  - Mn (lost to slag/leach residue, no battery-grade Mn recovery): ~0.08 kg/kWh
  - Separator + binders + carbon black: ~0.10 kg/kWh
  - Cell housing steel + tabs: ~0.10 kg/kWh
  - Module + pack structural Al/steel/plastic: ~1.70 kg/kWh
  - Process metal residues (5–15% of contained Li/Ni/Co not recovered): ~0.05 kg/kWh
  - Other (residual TM as oxide, contaminants, water from sludges): ~0.87 kg/kWh
  Sum ≈ 4.47 kg/kWh. Range 4.10–4.80 reflects pack-overhead recycling assumptions
  (low: more pack Al/steel diverted to metal scrap; high: more lost in slag/incineration).
PRIOR VALUE (compound-equivalent basis): 2.82 kg/kWh (F101–F103 reported as LiOH·H2O / NiSO4 / CoSO4 compound-equivalents). Updated 2026-04-30 to elemental basis for cleaner mass closure.
